original_question: Let Delta be a centrally symmetric simplicial sphere, so Delta admits a fixed-point-free involution alpha on its vertex set, and let Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d be a linear system of parameters chosen generically from S^- = {f in S : alpha(f) = -f}. With respect to the linear form w = x1 + ... + xn, does the Artinian reduction S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) always have the strong or weak Lefschetz property?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct open problem very closely: it uses a centrally symmetric simplicial sphere Delta, the fixed-point-free involution alpha, the anti-invariant choice of a linear system of parameters Theta from S^-, the Artinian reduction S/(I_Delta + (Theta)), the distinguished linear form w = x_1 + ... + x_n, and it asks exactly about the strong/weak Lefschetz property for that specific reduction.
missing_details: Section 4 fixes the ambient ring as S = K[x_1, ..., x_n], standard graded over a field K of characteristic zero.
The paper uses the Stanley-Reisner notation I_Delta and K[Delta] = S/I_Delta, with Delta on vertex set [n] = {1, ..., n}.
Centrally symmetric means not only that alpha is fixed-point-free on vertices, but also that alpha preserves the complex: Delta = {alpha(F) : F in Delta}.
The involution alpha must be extended to S by alpha(x_v) = x_{alpha(v)} in order for S^- = {f in S : alpha(f) = -f} to make sense.
Theta is required to be a linear system of parameters for K[Delta], not merely a generic anti-invariant sequence.
Because Theta is linear, the intended generic choice is from the degree-1 anti-invariant subspace (S^-)_1, even though the paper abbreviates this as taken from S^-.
The exact quantifier is for every centrally symmetric simplicial (d-1)-sphere Delta and every generic anti-invariant l.s.o.p. Theta in this sense.

The standard meanings of WLP and SLP with respect to the fixed linear form w are left implicit in the draft: WLP means multiplication by w has maximal rank in every degree, and SLP means multiplication by every power of w has maximal rank in every degree where it is defined.

The paper's surrounding context makes clear that this is a question about a specific structured l.s.o.p. and the specific Lefschetz element w, not about arbitrary generic l.s.o.p.'s; that distinction matters because Theorem 4.1 already settles the fully generic case for simplicial spheres.
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let S = K[x_1, ..., x_n] be the standard graded polynomial ring, and let Delta be a centrally symmetric simplicial (d-1)-sphere on vertex set [n] = {1, ..., n}; that is, Delta admits a fixed-point-free involution alpha:[n] -> [n] such that Delta = {alpha(F) : F in Delta}. Extend alpha to S by alpha(x_v) = x_{alpha(v)}, and write S^- = {f in S : alpha(f) = -f}. If Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d is a generic linear system of parameters for K[Delta] = S/I_Delta with each theta_i in the degree-1 anti-invariant subspace (S^-)_1, and if w = x_1 + ... + x_n, must the Artinian reduction A = S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) have the strong Lefschetz property with respect to w (that is, for every i >= 0 and j >= 1, multiplication by w^j induces a map A_i -> A_{i+j} of maximal rank), or at least the weak Lefschetz property with respect to w (that is, multiplication by w induces a map A_i -> A_{i+1} of maximal rank for every i >= 0)?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 4.3 in Section 4 exactly, not a broader neighboring question. Section 4 first fixes the notation S = K[x_1, ..., x_n] over a characteristic-zero field K, with Delta a simplicial complex on [n], and uses I_Delta and K[Delta] for the Stanley-Reisner ideal and ring. Immediately after Theorem 4.1, the subsection on centrally symmetric spheres defines the free Z/2Z-action via a fixed-point-free involution alpha, explains that one chooses an l.s.o.p. from the anti-invariant space S^-, and then states Problem 4.3 asking whether S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) has the SLP or WLP with respect to w = x_1 + ... + x_n. The nearby Theorem 4.1 is important context: it already gives the SLP for a generic l.s.o.p. on any simplicial sphere, so Problem 4.3 is specifically about whether this structured anti-invariant l.s.o.p. together with the specific element w still yields Lefschetz behavior. The refined version stays faithful to that exact intent and only spells out the paper's implicit standard conventions needed to make the question stand-alone.
